$comment: The parts of upstream's schemas left open (D13c decision 4; Preflight rulings 4, 6 and 7; the execution rulings), each with its reason: where upstream describes a setting wrongly or omits a key the collector reads (checked against the Go at the tag; a key the collector only ignores stays flagged), the built components upstream has no schema for, and every reference to a definition upstream never wrote. An entry names a definition (repository/package.definition, or repository/package for a file's root), a component (kind/type: only one upstream describes none of the settings of; a component with a schema is named by its schema), or a part of either (path: keys joined by '.', '[]' a list's items, '*' a map's values); versions limits it to those versions. 'unknown keys' keeps an object's settings and accepts any other key; 'any value' drops the type; 'any casing' accepts an enum's values in any casing; 'any string' keeps an enum's values as suggestions and accepts any string; 'strings take any scalar' lets every string setting the definition writes itself take a number or true/false too; 'a string too' keeps what upstream says and accepts a plain string as well; 'unknown keys in its place' drops the definition's own setting at path, which upstream named after a Go field tagged ,remain (a map of the object's other keys), and lets any other key of the object hold what that map's values are, wherever the definition is used or embedded. A definition's name ending in '*' names every definition of that file starting with what precedes it; a definition's path stays inside it, a component's goes through what it refers to. capitalisedKeys lists the settings upstream names with a capital letter that the collector reads by those names (a Go field tagged with no name; confmap matches names case-sensitively), under the definition the run names. generate-otelcol-schemas.ts stops on an entry a version it applies to doesn't use, on a component entry for a component upstream now has a schema with settings for, on a dangling reference or a setting named like a Go field (a capital first letter) not listed here, and, when an entry limited to other versions would answer, says to extend its versions.

upstream's schema omits receivers, which Config.Unmarshal reads by hand (receiver/receivercreator/config.go:118 at every offered version): each receivers.<type/name> holds a rule, resource_attributes and a config map that the receiver passes on to the receiver it creates. The open-parts list can't add a key, so receiver_creator's own settings are open to any key; a typo among them (discovry) goes unflagged until the validator answers.

upstream names a setting after the Go field ExtensionCfg, a map tagged mapstructure:",remain" that holds the policy's other keys (processor/tailsamplingprocessor/config.go:102, sharedPolicyCfg): a policy whose type is a policy extension's reads that extension's settings under its type's name (processor.go, getSharedPolicyEvaluator). So the policy takes any other key holding a map (what each extension's settings are): a typo among its settings holding a scalar (tpye: latency) still warns, one holding a map goes unflagged until the validator answers.

the receiver's config is upstream's hand-written copy of Prometheus's configuration, which omits scrape_config_files: Prometheus reads it and so does the receiver (PromConfig.ContainsScrapeConfigs, receiver/prometheusreceiver/config.go:77; PromConfig.Unmarshal hands the whole config to Prometheus's config.Load, config.go:84 and 187-198). The copy's other objects stay closed: Prometheus decodes them with yaml.UnmarshalStrict (config/config.go:81), so an unknown key there is refused at start.

the receiver marshals config back to YAML and Prometheus decodes it with go.yaml.in/yaml/v2 v2.4.4 (the receiver pins github.com/prometheus/prometheus v0.313.2 (v3.13.2) at 0.159.0 and v0.314.0 (v3.14.0) from 0.160.0, the same code at both), whose decoder sets a Go string from any non-null scalar's text (decode.go:411, decoder.scalar, reflect.String), so job_name: 5 or replacement: true is read as text.

Prometheus lowercases a relabel action before checking it (model/relabel/relabel.go:72-82, Action.UnmarshalYAML; the receiver pins github.com/prometheus/prometheus v0.313.2 (v3.13.2) at 0.159.0 and v0.314.0 (v3.14.0) from 0.160.0, the same code at both), so Keep and KEEP are read as keep.

scheme is a plain string Prometheus never checks at load (config/config.go:800; the receiver pins github.com/prometheus/prometheus v0.313.2 (v3.13.2) at 0.159.0 and v0.314.0 (v3.14.0) from 0.160.0, the same code at both); http and https are its usual values.
